summary: Intermittent API proxy panic + runtime throttle causing elevated 5xx for a dedicated tenant during warmup
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 08:20 UTC, a single dedicated tenant (Eunoia Health) experienced a burst of 5xx errors across chat and embeddings routes. Symptoms include intermittent API gateway 'proxy panic: accept queue closed' logs and downstream serving-runtime exits with SIGABRT during GPU warmup. Impact: customer reports ~40% failure rate for requests to their pinned model, causing feature regressions in their product. Environment: prod-us-east-1, dedicated pool assigned to tenant.

Impact: High - customer-facing features degraded for a paid dedicated tenant.

Observed behavior: API gateway returns 502/503 for a subset of streaming and short-request chat calls. Upstream runtime processes show abrupt exits and kernel swap logs. Errors spike correlated with autoscaler adding warmup instances for the tenant during a scheduled traffic ramp.

Why this ticket: Customer opened a support request after seeing elevated error rates and intermittent connection resets. We need triage, mitigation, and an RCA.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate tenant traffic ramp targeting their dedicated pool (sustained 200 qps over 3 minutes)
2) Observe autoscaler scaling events and warmup tasks in prod-us-east-1
3) Monitor api-gateway logs for 'accept queue closed' and serving-runtime logs for SIGABRT entries
4) Repeat with model variants (rwkv-13b and gpt-rev-3.5-v2 pinned) to check model-specific failure modes
logs_and_metrics_summary: api-gateway: repeated 'proxy panic: accept queue closed' in /var/log/apigw/2026-03-13.log around 08:21-08:35 UTC
serving-runtime: abrupt exits with SIGABRT and backtrace showing nvml driver calls during model load (see runtime stderr snippets)
autoscaler: launched 6 warmup instances for tenant between 08:19-08:24 UTC, several timed out on prewarm checks
cloud-metrics: GPU allocation spikes + kernel swap events on nodes hosting tenant warmups
observability: customer error rate rose from 0.8% to 42% during the window; p50 latency increased 2.3x
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - Support triaged with SRE: correlation between warmup launches and first 5xx spike. (Aisha)
2026-03-13 10:05 UTC - SRE captured core dumps from two runtimes; backtraces indicate NVML callsite failures during driver init. (Marco)
Hypothesis A: GPU driver interaction during concurrent prewarm + model load is triggering a rare nvml assertion leading to process abort and subsequent proxy panics when accept queues back up.
Hypothesis B: API gateway accept-queue thresholds are too low for sudden warmup fan-in and amplify upstream restarts into 502 waves.
Observed a pattern where failed warmups caused connection handoffs and backpressure, producing the 'accept queue closed' panic in the proxy code path.
customer_communication: 2026-03-13 09:15 UTC - Aisha Khan (Support) to Eunoia Health: We see elevated 5xx in your dedicated pool; we're investigating and have temporarily increased prewarm timeouts to reduce aborts. (Acknowledged)

2026-03-13 11:30 UTC - Marco Li (SRE) to Eunoia Health: We're routing new requests away from affected warmup hosts and throttling simultaneous prewarm jobs while we gather artifacts. Please expect intermittent errors to continue for a short window. (Ack)
Customer response: Confirmed reduced user impact after routing change; still seeing occasional timeouts on long-poll streams.
mitigation_actions: Immediate: Adjusted autoscaler prewarm concurrency to 2 for the tenant to avoid simultaneous model loads on the same node (rolled at 08:40 UTC)
Immediate: Increased api-gateway accept-queue size and added temporary rate-limiter exception for the tenant's control plane calls to reduce accept-queue closure panics (08:50 UTC)
Workaround: Routed traffic for the tenant to warm pool nodes that completed model load successfully; this reduced observed 5xx from ~42% -> ~8% within 20 minutes
open_actions_and_followups: Collect and analyze all core dumps and NVML traces from affected nodes (owner: Marco, due 2026-03-15)
Run targeted load/repro test in staging replicating warmup concurrency and GPU driver version; capture deterministic repro (owner: Runtime team, due 2026-03-17)
Propose autoscaler change: introduce jittered warmup scheduling and cap concurrent warmups per physical host (owner: Scheduler team, due 2026-03-22)
Add a proxy hardening item: handle accept-queue closure without triggering full panic and instead return 503 with graceful drain (owner: API gateway team, due 2026-03-20)
Customer follow-up: arrange a postmortem and discuss SLA credits if thresholds met (owner: CS Manager Maya Patel, due 2026-03-18)
Security/Compliance: ensure artifact collection does not include PII before sharing with customer; scrub logs.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigation in place: routing and prewarm concurrency limits reduced customer impact and lowered error rate. Root cause investigation ongoing (NVML interaction under high concurrent model-load pressure). No permanent fix deployed as of update date. Final RCA and permanent remediation plan will be attached to this ticket once validated.
